why: Flaws in this package, deposited here because the live write channels do not retain one. Measured, both of them: POST /message answers 202 and mints a uuid for a message its own reading says it keeps `never` — the lanes are isolate memory and a GET afterwards returns the catalog; /storage refuses without QPU_WRITE_TOKEN, which is the owner's to set. ONE FILE, because two were a convention fork: a second deposit beside the first is a second place to look and a second schema to drift, and the gatherer globbed both only by luck of naming. Every row carries the session that found it, so merging loses no provenance.

channels_tried.result: 202 accepted, uuid 00000001-0001-1001-8001-001c00000002, lane 1 — and the reading itself says when: never, await: false. The lanes are isolate memory; a GET afterwards returns the catalog, not the message. It imprints a UUID for a message it does not keep.
refused without QPU_WRITE_TOKEN, which is the owner's to set — unchanged since the 2026-09-28 uuidna deposit recorded the same thing.

flaws.measured: The v0.1.5 publish run FAILED for e3cc72dffa01ddcd53f535e96229a5180435fc82, while npm itself succeeded: the registry serves 0.1.5 as latest, dist.attestations carries SLSA provenance, and gitHead equals the v0.1.5 tag commit. verify-release reports 4 of 5 green and names the fifth — Zenodo still holds v0.1.4 after 30 rounds.
flaws.reading: The failure is DOWNSTREAM of publishing. publish.yml's own comment says it does three things and confirms none of them; verify-release is the arm that confirms, so a failed run beside a live package means the release is LIVE and INCOMPLETE. A run status alone cannot tell those two apart, which is the thing worth fixing: the run should say which of the five checks it failed.
flaws.owes: Distinguish a webhook that fired late from one that never fired — ask Zenodo by concept DOI after the run, not inside it.

flaws.state: FIXED 2026-09-29 — scripts/chain.test.mjs now checks both directions: every step npm run ci names is reachable from ci.yml, and every gate step ci.yml runs is in npm run ci or named in CI_ONLY with its reason (debts, outage). The pre-push hook runs npm run ci itself (scripts/pre-push.sh).
flaws.measured: package.json ci = lean && test && proof && mutate && test:scripts. No workflow invokes it; ci.yml re-lists the steps by hand. Before this session ci.yml named ONE scripts test (outage:test), so the leads, pace, percall and temporal suites ran in no chain at all — four of five guard suites unreachable while the board was green. All five pass; they were never asked.
flaws.reading: A list somebody edits is a list somebody forgets. The discovery half is cured — ci.yml now runs test:scripts, which globs scripts/*.test.mjs, so a suite added tomorrow runs the day it exists.
flaws.owes: The duplication between `npm run ci` and ci.yml is two hand lists that must agree and nothing checks that they do.

flaws.measured: In a clean install of the published 0.1.5 tarball with no network, 14 of 101 *Holds predicates do not hold. qpuApisLiveHolds, qpuCitationsLiveHolds, qpuComposeHolds, qpuComposeLiveHolds and qpuCrossHolds throw 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading holds)'; qpuCiteHolds returns false.
flaws.reading: A consumer importing the package offline receives a TypeError from an internal rather than a refusal naming the missing instrument. qpu's own kernelPresent() carries the right law: an absent instrument VOIDS the judgement and says so by name, because a trial whose instrument is missing carries no information about the subject.
flaws.owes: NOT VERIFIED against a live-host run — the in-context suite passes 173/173, so this is reported as a shape, not a verdict.

flaws.measured: uuidna's kernel-probe writes lean/_wave_probe.<pid>.lean, and its suite runs --test-isolation=none, so every test shares one pid: two probe() calls resolve to one path and each unlinks under the other. Seen as ENOENT inside a landing's clean worktree while passing standalone.
flaws.reading: This is uuidna's defect, reported here because qpu carries the same probe pattern and the same 'one probe file per process' comment. A green that holds only while nothing else probes is not a green.
flaws.owes: Cured in uuidna with a per-call counter — deterministic, no clock and no random. qpu should check whether its own probe paths are per-call rather than per-process.

flaws.measured: faf8e51 shipped four sitemaps listing https://<sibling>.uuidna.com/.well-known/mcp.json on hosts that answered 404 for it. The test above the predicate said a listed URL must be one this unit can answer; the predicate only checked the URL's HOST. Green the whole time.
flaws.reading: A predicate weaker than the sentence it sits under is worse than no predicate, because the sentence is what a reader trusts. The check now fetches every <loc>.
flaws.owes: nothing — the discovery record is served on every routed host and every <loc> was verified 200 live.

flaws.measured: qpuSeoZoneOf computed robots.txt and sitemap.xml for uuidna.com. This worker holds qpu.uuidna.com and the *.uuidna.com wildcard; the apex is under neither, and already serves its own robots.txt and an 11,438-URL sitemap from the worker that does hold it. The sitemap produced here listed a root this unit answers 404 for.
flaws.reading: A table that says what the zone IS is not a table of what this unit SERVES. Each zone row now carries `qpu`, and the reading filters on it.

flaws.state: OPEN — not this unit's to settle
flaws.measured: lean, unreal, hardware and school under uuidna.com all answer with `x-powered-by: Next.js, Payload`, i.e. this unit's wildcard route forwards them to Payload as tenant sites. Meanwhile lean/wrangler.toml and unreal/wrangler.toml each declare `custom_domain = true` for those exact names, and those workers' own doors — /nav, /standing, /mcp, /sitemap.xml — exist in their source and answer 404 on the live hosts.
flaws.reading: Two declarations disagree about who serves four live names, and the one that is winning is not the one written down. Computing `reserved` from the zone table would have pulled all four out of the tenant forward and turned four live 200s into 404s; that was caught by cancelling a deploy mid-flight, not by a test.
flaws.owes: whoever owns those routes decides: either the sibling workers take their hosts back, or their wrangler.toml stops claiming them. Until then this unit takes only /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and /.well-known/mcp.json on those names and forwards everything else exactly as before.

flaws.measured: Before this work, five of six first-party hosts answered 404 for /robots.txt, and the zone's managed default was served in their place — a file naming no sitemap. qpu.uuidna.com had been computing a real sitemap at /sitemap.xml the whole time and nothing pointed at it.
flaws.reading: A 404 on a discovery path is not an absence a reader sees; it is a substitution a reader believes. Any NEW host added to this zone will ship the same default until it is added to QPU_ZONE_HOSTS.
flaws.owes: a detector that asks each host for its pair and fails when the answer is the managed default rather than this unit's.

flaws.measured: payload's node_modules copy of @uuidna/uuidna was a 2026-09-27 snapshot, 1187 files against the source's 1253, and every one of payload's fifteen integration spec files failed at import with `Cannot find module .../dist/artifact.js`. scripts/leads.mjs already has copyLeadsOf, which detects exactly this and reports it green now that the copy was refreshed.
flaws.reading: The detector was right and nobody ran it. pnpm copies a file: dependency instead of linking it, so the copy freezes at install time and the symptom arrives as a missing module in an unrelated repository.
flaws.owes: payload's own suite should ask before it runs, or this gatherer should run in payload's CI; a detector in one repository does not protect another.

flaws.measured: On the hosted uuidna MCP, list_tools {query} returns [] for every multi-word query tried — "message send agent coordinate flaw report", and for the single words "messaging" and "improve" — while "gate" returns six tools. get_server_status advertises a messaging witness with 2127 keys, and no tool's name or description contains the word.
flaws.reading: A search that answers nothing for a natural-language query is read as 'no such tool exists' rather than 'no tool matched every word'. The empty result carries no hint that relaxing the query would help.
flaws.owes: either rank partial matches instead of requiring all terms, or say which terms matched nothing — an empty list is the one answer that cannot be acted on.

flaws.measured: uuidna/src/hex-programs.ts uuidOfCall({handle:'deadbeef', door:'uuidna_aas', params:'0001', envelope:'aabbccddeeff'}) returns deadbeef-ab99-b62a-0001-aabbccddeeff. The version nibble is 'b' and the variant nibble is '0'; RFC 9562 admits versions 1-8 and variants 8-b. It round-trips through callOfUuid correctly, so nothing there notices.
flaws.reading: The 48-bit middle cannot hold 32 bits of door and 16 of params AND stay a UUID, because RFC 9562 spends one nibble of that middle on the version and one on the variant. Forty bits are addressable, not forty-eight. qpu's own qpuShapeUuidHolds refuses exactly this shape, which is why the combinatorial address here takes 16 bits of door and 12 of params and keeps v8 valid.
flaws.owes: either reserve the two nibbles and drop to 40 addressable bits, or stop calling the result a UUID — a consumer that validates one will reject every address this mints.

flaws.measured: In uuidna, callOfUuid and uuidOfCall appear in src/mcp.ts only inside comments. resolveToolName re-implements the decode inline — bare.slice(8, 16) then a lookup — rather than calling callOfUuid, which is the third derivation of that slice in the tree and the exact drift callOfUuid's own comment warns about for handleOf. hexProgramOf and collisionsOf have no caller outside their own module either.
flaws.reading: The commit that wired the codec in wrote that a consumer check had found zero real callers, and then added a fourth non-caller. A codec reachable only from its own suite is dead code with a passing test.
flaws.owes: resolveToolName should call callOfUuid; uuidOfCall needs a caller that mints an address somebody reads, or it should go.
